facts.subject: CRIF lobbying status
facts.value: HATVP registers CRIF as an interest representative and records its activities as representation of interests carried out for its own account.

facts.subject: CRIF policy access
facts.value: CRIF declarations document meetings, events, hearings, expertise and suggestions intended to influence public decisions, including antisemitism-policy work and parliamentary/government targets.

facts.subject: ELNET France lobbying status
facts.value: HATVP registers ELNET France as an interest representative acting for its own account, with declared contacts/actions targeting presidential, parliamentary and ministerial officials.

facts.subject: ELNET France Palestine recognition objective
facts.value: ELNET France declared a 2025 lobbying objective to oppose French recognition of the State of Palestine, using meetings/events and targeting national decision-makers.

facts.subject: AJC France access
facts.value: AJC France declarations show own-account interest representation including invitation to the 2025 Assises against antisemitism, a Senate colloquium on Zionism/France/Israel and a parliamentary audition on European cooperation against antisemitism.

facts.subject: CRIF IHRA request
facts.value: At the 20 February 2019 CRIF dinner, Francis Kalifat explicitly argued that France needed the IHRA working definition and asked for stronger state action against antisemitism.

facts.subject: Macron IHRA response
facts.value: At the same CRIF dinner, Emmanuel Macron announced that France would implement the IHRA working definition while explicitly stating that this would not modify the Penal Code.

facts.subject: Assembly IHRA vote
facts.value: The National Assembly adopted the resolution against antisemitism on 3 December 2019 by 154 votes to 72, with 43 abstentions.

facts.subject: Pre-existing parliamentary IHRA initiative
facts.value: Sylvain Maillard states that on 19 February 2019, one day before the CRIF dinner, he had already convened the parliamentary antisemitism study group to propose transcribing the IHRA working definition and later thanked Macron for taking up that proposal.

facts.subject: IHRA parliamentary process
facts.value: Maillard described the resolution as the product of more than two years of transpartisan group work with 130 co-signatories and stated that the resolution was not legally binding and did not modify the Penal Code or the 1881 press law.

facts.subject: Israeli MFA funding of ELNET Europe event
facts.value: An Israeli government procurement notice identifies the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as publisher, ELNET Europe-Israel as sole supplier, EUR 72,000 as amount and 10 November 2025 as the one-day engagement date for a conference at the French Senate.

facts.subject: Yadan bill filing
facts.value: Caroline Yadan and co-authors filed proposal no. 575 on 19 November 2024 to address renewed forms of antisemitism.

facts.subject: Yadan bill withdrawal
facts.value: On 16 April 2026, parliamentary debate recorded that Caroline Yadan withdrew her proposal and that a government transpartisan successor bill would be filed.

facts.subject: Successor government bill provenance
facts.value: The Conseil d’État states that the 2026 government bill continues the 2023-2026 national plan and the 2025 Assises and follows multiple parliamentary initiatives, including but not limited to Yadan proposal no. 575.

facts.subject: France recognition of Palestine
facts.value: On 22 September 2025, Emmanuel Macron formally declared that France recognized the State of Palestine.

facts.subject: French restrictions on Israeli officials and settlers
facts.value: France stated that it imposed entry bans on Israeli ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, four settlement leaders and other violent settlers, alongside European sanctions.
